links.outcome: LLM DDI identification accuracy against a database-derived reference standard (sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1)
links.effect: Against 204 reference DDIs, ChatGPT flagged 439, Gemini 1556, Copilot 1813. Gemini sensitivity 0.697; ChatGPT specificity 0.868; F1 0.2520 (ChatGPT), 0.1933 (Gemini), 0.1153 (Copilot); precision low.
links.quote: Our results suggest that no AI systems assessed achieve the required balance of precision and sensitivity for reliable clinical decision-making in DDI screening.

links.outcome: Incorrect or hallucinated LLM interaction outputs that clinicians would need to verify
links.effect: All three LLMs had low precision and flagged many more interactions than the 204 in the reference set (439, 1556, 1813), producing clinically inaccurate information from hallucinations.
links.quote: Although LLMs show promise as complementary tools in DDI screening, as they proved effective in identifying true interactions, they generate clinically inaccurate information due to hallucinations, which limits their reliability as standalone screening tools.

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot) on retrospective real-world medication lists for drug-drug interaction detection compared to reference databases, evaluating performance without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
